title: Adaptive shadow & border semantics for brand-aware dark surfaces
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Our current dark mode token set flattens shadows and borders across brands, causing low contrast or visual noise for customers that use bold brand accents. Goal: Define a minimal semantic mapping for shadows and borders in dark surfaces that is brand-aware, easy for engineers to consume, and safe for backward-compatible rollouts. Scope: (1) token-level mapping for elevation-shadow and border tokens; (2) component overrides for Button, Table rows, Chart axes & gridlines, Tooltip/Popover; (3) fallback rules when brand palette lacks sufficient contrast; (4) runtime flags for staggered rollout and canary testing on Dedicated/Hosted consoles.
acceptance_criteria: A semantic token spec (.fig) for shadow and border roles in dark mode that maps to brand palettes with 3 contrast tiers
Component-level override examples (Button primary/ghost, Table header/row hover, Chart axis/grid, Tooltip) implemented in Storybook with visual diff tests
Engineers can toggle brand-aware shadows via a single feature flag; default preserves current appearance for customers not opted-in
Confluence PR with rollout plan, accessibility contrast notes, and automated QA checklist published
Design handoff Figma frames and CSS variables provided with usage guidance and migration notes
design_notes: Use semantic role names (surface-shadow-low/surface-shadow-medium/surface-shadow-high) instead of brand-specific shadow tokens to minimize cognitive load for engineers
Prefer low-opacity color overlays over heavier multi-layered shadows to reduce GPU cost on lower-end devices
For brand-heavy consoles, introduce a subtle colored rim border (<=1px) derived from brand accent at 12% opacity to maintain brand presence without harming contrast
Decision: avoid introducing new elevation scale numbers; map to existing elevation indices (e0-e4) with dark-mode remapping
Trade-off: stronger colored shadows increase perceived vibrancy but may create contrast regressions for small text — we will gate stronger effects behind an opt-in flag
